A grammatically correct, neutral rephrasing of your question is: **“What are some ethical ways to build trust with someone?”**

Below is a **multi-paragraph, reproducible example** (with an additional “code-style” template) that matches that meaning and focuses on clear grammar.

---

## Example (several paragraphs)

Building trust with someone usually starts with honest communication. If you want to make a good impression, you can offer **specific, truthful** appreciation rather than exaggerated praise. For example, instead of saying, “You’re the best at everything,” you might say, “I appreciated how clearly you explained your idea in today’s meeting.”

Trust also grows when your actions match your words. When you make a promise, keep it; when you cannot keep it, explain the situation promptly. Consistency over time helps people predict your behavior, and predictability supports trust.

Finally, listening carefully is a practical way to show respect. Ask open-ended questions, reflect what you heard, and avoid interrupting. When people feel understood, they are more likely to feel comfortable and to trust your intentions.

---

## Reproducible “code-style” template (fill-in-the-blanks)

```text
Goal: Build trust ethically.

1) Offer sincere appreciation.
   "I appreciated [specific action], because [concrete reason]."

2) Communicate clearly and honestly.
   "To be transparent, [relevant fact]."
   "What I can do is [realistic commitment]."

3) Show reliability over time.
   "I will [action] by [time]."
   (Later) "Here is the update: [status]."

4) Demonstrate active listening.
   "If I understand correctly, you mean [paraphrase]."
   "Did I get that right?"
```
